newsitem.title: ZIMBABWE: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CLOSES WEAKER AHEAD OF BUDGET.
newsitem.headline: ZIMBABWE DOLLAR CLOSES WEAKER AHEAD OF BUDGET.

text.p: The Zimbabwe dollar closed on Thursday weaker on the key U.S. dollar ahead of a national budget announcement but foreign exchange dealers disclaimed any linkage between the two.

They said said the depreciation was caused mainly by a big import payment which went out of the system on Wednesday and left the market about Z$80 million short, driving most banks into panic buying and quoting wide bid/offer spreads to protect their positions.

"It's just a co-incidence that this (fall) happened around budget time," said one, reiterating earlier assertions by his colleagues that the local unit was mainly driven by forces of demand and supply.
"We don't expect any surprises in the budget that would move the exchange rates," another added.
The local unit ended the day at 11.5000/6000 compared to late Wednesday's 11.4500/4600 but was firmer against sterling at 19.1305/1505 from 19.2200/2350, tracking a firmer U.S. dollar overseas.
It was at 6.2230/2300 against the mark from 6.2600/2700 but was weaker at 2.5050/5105 from 2.4900/5150 against South Africa's rand.
